overview: This 572-page file traces Japan’s 1949 effort to become economically self-supporting. Diplomatic reports, speeches, surveys, and economic studies examine a five-year rehabilitation plan, exports, U.S. aid, and the Dodge stabilization program. Japanese, American, and British assessments document the tension between curbing inflation and sustaining investment, production, employment, and living standards.
interest: Extensive Japanese studies and public opinion data reveal how officials and citizens experienced the costs of stabilization.
